body.question: Why do leaves look green?
options: Leaves absorb green light and reflect blue
Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light, so green is absorbed less and scattered back
body.reveal: Chlorophyll absorbs strongly in the blue and red parts of the spectrum and is a poor absorber of green. Green light, reflected by structures like cell walls, is less absorbed, so leaves look green. Green is what is left over.

claims.claim: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly blue and red; green is less absorbed and reflected by structures like cell walls (answer and reveal)
claims.quote: Plants are perceived as green because chlorophyll absorbs mainly the blue and red wavelengths but green light, reflected by plant structures like cell walls, is less absorbed.

claims.claim: Chlorophyll absorbs most strongly in blue and red (probe 1 answer)
claims.quote: Chlorophylls absorb light most strongly in the blue and red portions of the electromagnetic spectrum .

claims.claim: Chlorophyll is a poor absorber of green
claims.quote: Conversely, it is a poor absorber of green and near-green portions of the spectrum.
